messages:

Subject: Tenant on-prem attachment — initial diagrams and questions

Hi Diego / Kimberly,

Attaching our initial VPC/attachment diagrams for tenant ACME-42. We're planning an on-prem attachment that routes inference traffic to Redwood's private control plane and keeps model artifacts in our colo. High-level ask: can Redwood review the control-plane/data-plane boundaries and confirm any egress requirements or proxy expectations?

Attachments: edgecloud_vpc_diagram_v1.pdf (pdf) — topology and cross-connects

Key notes / open questions:
- Do you require a dedicated control-plane API endpoint inside the tenant VPC, or can the control plane be fronted via a regional relay?
- Expected NAT / source-IP expectations for telemetry and health checks?
- Any specific mTLS SNI or header expectations on the data-plane handshake?

We'd like a short readout next week before the colo team starts cross-connect provisioning.

Thanks,
Raj Patel
EdgeCloud — Network Engineering
ops@edgecloud.io
From: Diego Fernández <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant on-prem attachment — initial diagrams and questions

Hi Raj — thanks for the diagrams, we got them. I've looped in Mateo and Kimberly from infra and networking.

Quick answers up front:
- Control plane: we prefer a pinned, tenant-dedicated control-plane endpoint inside your VPC (private IP + customer-managed routing) for low-latency registry/rollout calls, but we can support a regional relay if you need to avoid inbound peering.
- NAT/source IPs: Redwood will emit telemetry from a small set of egress IPs. We will provide a CIDR block for allowlisting; health checks can come from the same range.
- mTLS: we require mutual TLS for data-plane KV-cache priming and artifact fetches. SNI is optional but helpful — we can accept SAN-based certs and support a single cert per attachment.

I've attached an internal checklist and our suggested minimal demarc notes (redwood_demarc_checklist.xlsx). Can the EdgeCloud team confirm whether the colo will NAT outbound, or preserve source IPs? That will affect our telemetry and audit logs.

Proposed next step: 45-min sync tomorrow 10:00am PT to walk the diagram and acceptance criteria. Please confirm.

Thanks,
Diego Fernández
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
redwood.com | diego.fernandez@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: notes on EdgeCloud diagram (control/data boundaries)

Diego / Mateo — quick internal readout before tomorrow's sync. Forwarding Raj's diagram excerpt below for context.

On Tue, 20 Jun 2028 at 09:12 AM EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.io> wrote:
> Attaching our initial VPC/attachment diagrams for tenant ACME-42...

Observations / proposed changes:
- Control plane placement: we should avoid exposing the full control plane into their management VLAN. Propose a small control-plane relay (3 VM) in a management subnet with strict ACLs (only Redwood outbound to control-plane management endpoints).
- Data plane (inference path) should terminate in their private inference subnet; we will run the runtime nodes in their colo and use an encrypted peer to Redwood for model sync. KV cache priming must be one-way (EdgeCloud -> Redwood) and not accept inbound config pushes from the public internet.
- Egress: telemetry and metrics must egress to Redwood via NAT with preserved source mapping if possible; fallback is SNAT with allowlisted CIDR from Redwood's side.
- Certs: recommend an automated cert rotation model using their KMS and our CA signing. We'll note this in the runbook.

Open items for Mateo:
- Can you confirm expected MTU and any jumbo-frame needs? The diagram shows 9000MTU cross-connect; we need to validate for NVMe transfers during model sync.
- Can you propose a minimal ACL list (src/dst/port) we can share with EdgeCloud?

I'll compile our answers and draft a lean diagram overlay for tomorrow.

---
Kimberly Park
Infrastructure PM — Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernández <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.io>, SableCorp NetOps <netops@sablecorp.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant on-prem attachment — initial diagrams and questions (Redwood comments & next steps)

Hi Raj / SableCorp team — thanks for the patience. Following our internal review and the sync earlier today, attached are Redwood's annotated items and the minimal acceptance checklist. High level summary below.

Attachments: redwood_demarc_notes_v2.pdf (annotated diagram), redwood_demarc_checklist.xlsx (runbook checklist)

Redwood comments (actionable):
1) Control-plane: preferred model is tenant-dedicated control-plane endpoint inside the VPC (private IP). If you cannot provision inbound peering, we will accept a regional relay but will require a static tunnel and a service-account allowlist.
2) Data-plane: inference nodes stay in tenant colo. Model sync uses TLS + mutual auth over the dedicated tunnel. Ensure the cross-connect preserves MTU >= 9000 for bulk pulls; if not, we will chunk artifact transfers and throttle accordingly.
3) Egress & telemetry: please preserve source IPs for audit accuracy. If preserve is impossible, confirm SNAT blocks and we'll add mapping in our observability. Provide expected egress CIDR by Friday.
4) Port/ACL baseline (minimal):
   - Control-plane API: TCP 443 (HTTPS, mTLS optional) -> control-plane endpoint
   - Model/artifact fetch: TCP 443 (TLS) outbound to Redwood artifact gateway
   - Health & telemetry: TCP 443 outbound to telemetry ingestion (Redwood egress IPs)
   - KV priming: TCP 443 with client cert; one-way from tenant to Redwood

4) Certs: recommend KMS-backed certs. We'll provide CSR template and rotation cadence (90 days) if you want Redwood to sign.

Next steps / asks from EdgeCloud/SableCorp by EOD Friday:
- Confirm whether cross-connect will preserve source-IP (yes/no + if no, list SNAT CIDRs)
- Confirm MTU on the colo link
- Share SAML or service-account for relay auth if regional relay option is required

We can run a dry-run validation in your staging colo once the ACLs and routing are in place. Thanks — we'll keep the change list minimal to avoid rework during provisioning.

Best,
Diego Fernández
